extracted.intended_audience: insured depository institutions (national/state banks, savings associations, federal/state branches), bank compliance officers, bank legal counsel, and other CRA stakeholders (commenters, agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Interim final rule and technical amendments implementing changes to the 2023 CRA Final Rule, including extending applicability dates for facility-based assessment areas and public file provisions, updating cross-references, and adjusting asset-size thresholds to facilitate transition and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA good-cause exception for notice-and-comment and 30-day delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Procedure Act generally requires notice-and-comment and rules be published not less than 30 days before their effective date, but provides that these requirements do not apply “when the agency for good cause finds (and incorporates the finding and a brief statement of reasons therefor in the rules issued) that notice and public procedure thereon are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.” The 30-day delay before the effective date also has statutory exceptions (e.g., substantive rules which grant or recognize an exemption or relieve a restriction; interpretative rules and statements of policy; or as otherwise provided by the agency for good cause found and published with the rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies determined there is good cause to adopt the interim final rule and technical amendments without advance notice and comment and with less than 30 days before the effective date because the relief is time-sensitive (needed on or before April 1, 2024), would facilitate understanding and compliance, and is impracticable or contrary to the public interest to delay. Agencies incorporated brief statements of reasons in the rule's preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of applicability date for facility-based assessment areas and public file provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment extends applicability date of § __.16 (Facility-based assessment areas) and § __.43 (Content and availability of public file) from April 1, 2024, to January 1, 2026 (and aligns § __.44 applicability accordingly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies state the extension will facilitate bank understanding and compliance, allay uncertainty, and secure a stable transition from legacy CRA regulations to the 2023 CRA Final Rule. Although agencies find good cause to make the extension effective April 1, 2024, they are requesting public comment on moving the applicability date from April 1, 2024 to January 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice posting requirement (Section __.44 and CRA Notice form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.44 requires a bank to provide a CRA Notice in the public area of its main office and each of its branches, as set forth in appendix F, that includes information about availability of the bank's public file, the appropriate Federal financial supervisory agency's CRA examination schedule, and how a member of the public may provide public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because appendix F (the CRA Notice form reproduced in the 2023 CRA Final Rule) does not apply until January 1, 2026, the agencies amended § __.51(a)(2)(i) to align applicability so banks may continue to use the CRA Notice in the agencies' legacy CRA regulations (reproduced in appendix G) to comply with public notice requirements until January 1, 2026. The amendment is characterized as technical with no substantive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility-based assessment areas delineation standards (§ __.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.16(c) provides that facility-based assessment areas may not reflect illegal discrimination and may not arbitrarily exclude low- or moderate-income census tracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compared to the legacy CRA regulations, § __.16 requires certain changes to requirements for delineating CRA assessment areas based on a bank's deposit-taking facilities; the agencies extended applicability to allow time for banks to understand and comply with these changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public file content and availability adjustments (§ __.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.43 requires banks to make certain adjustments to comply with changes to public file requirements under the 2023 CRA Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these public-file provisions were originally applicable April 1, 2024, the agencies extended their applicability to January 1, 2026 to facilitate compliance and avoid uncertainty; agencies seek comment on the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/scope of 'bank' for this rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the Supplementary Information, the term 'bank' includes insured national and State banks, Federal and State savings associations, Federal branches (12 CFR part 28), insured State branches (12 CFR 345.11(c)), and State member banks (12 CFR part 208), except as provided in 12 CFR __.11(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inclusive definition clarifies which institutions the preamble's discussion and the transition provisions address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset-size thresholds for small and intermediate small banks
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated thresholds: (1) small banks: less than $1.564 billion in assets as of December 31 of either of the prior two calendar years; (2) intermediate small banks: at least $391 million as of December 31 of both of the prior two calendar years and less than $1.564 billion as of December 31 of either of the prior two calendar years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds reflect year-to-year CPI-W inflation adjustment pursuant to the legacy CRA regulations; the Board and FDIC updated appendix G so appendix G remains consistent with their legacy CRA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix G as the transitional repository of legacy CRA regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix G to the 2023 CRA Final Rule reproduces the agencies' legacy CRA regulations as of the date the agencies adopted the 2023 CRA Final Rule (October 24, 2023) and those legacy provisions apply to banks until superseded by provisions of the 2023 CRA Final Rule that become applicable on January 1, 2026, or January 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will update appendix G (e.g., asset-size thresholds and cross-references) so it remains accurate and consistent with legacy regulations during the transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities given favorable CRA consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing the following activities of the type likely to receive favorable consideration by a Federal banking agency in evaluating CRA performance: (i) home-purchase, home-improvement, small business, small farm, community development, and consumer lending (including loan purchases, loan commitments, and letters of credit); (ii) making investments, deposits, or grants, or acquiring membership shares primarily for community development; (iii) delivering retail banking services; (iv) providing community development services; (v) for wholesale or limited-purpose institutions: community development lending, qualified investments, or community development services; (vi) for small insured depository institutions: any lending or other activity described in the small-bank provisions; and (vii) for institutions evaluated on a strategic plan: any element of the strategic plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are described in the agencies' legacy regulations reproduced in appendix G and are referenced across parts implementing disclosure and reporting of CRA-related agreements (e.g., §§ 35.4, 207.4, 346.4). Specific cross-referenced appendix G sections provide detailed descriptions (e.g., § 25.22, § 25.23, § 25.24(d)/(e), § 25.25(c), § 25.26(a), § 25.27(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/conforming amendments and cross-reference updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies are making technical amendments to correct cross-references and conform citation language across multiple parts (e.g., updating CRA Sunshine regulations, OCC Public Welfare Investment regulation 12 CFR part 24, corrections in amendatory instructions, replacing outdated references to "the Federal Reserve" with "the Board," and updating cross-references from repealed parts to current parts such as changing references from part 195 to part 25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies state these technical amendments do not change the substance or meaning of the 2023 CRA Final Rule and are necessary to prevent inaccurate citations as of April 1, 2024. The agencies find good cause that public comment on these technical amendments is unnecessary and that less than 30 days before the effective date is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, no agency may conduct or sponsor an information collection without a currently valid OMB control number. The agencies determined that the interim final rule and technical amendments do not create any new or revise any existing collections of information pursuant to the PRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no new PRA collections are created or revised, no OMB control number issues arise from this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) applicability and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA requires an agency to provide a final regulatory flexibility analysis with a final rule unless the head of the agency certifies the rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities and publishes the certification and factual basis. The RFA does not apply to a rulemaking when a general notice of proposed rulemaking is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agencies determined that general notice of proposed rulemaking was not required for this interim final rule or the technical amendments; accordingly, RFA requirements relating to initial and final regulatory flexibility analyses do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riegle Community Development and Regulatory Improvement Act (RCDRIA) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 302(a) and (b) of RCDRIA, agencies must consider administrative burdens on depository institutions (including small institutions) and benefits of the rule, and new regulations imposing additional reporting, disclosure, or other new requirements on insured depository institutions generally must take effect on the first day of a calendar quarter following publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim final rule and technical amendments do not impose additional reporting, disclosure, or other new requirements; therefore subsections (a) and (b) are not applicable. The amendments are effective April 1, 2024 (first day of a calendar quarter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 722(a) of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act requires each Federal banking agency to use plain language in its proposed and final rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agencies state they used plain language in this document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: UMRA requires preparation of a budgetary impact statement before promulgating a rule that includes a Federal mandate that may result in expenditures of $100 million or more in any one year; UMRA does not apply to final rules for which a general notice of proposed rulemaking was not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the agencies found good cause for an exception to APA notice-and-comment, the OCC did not prepare an economic analysis under UMRA for these amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) major rule determination process
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the Congressional Review Act, OMB determines whether a final rule constitutes a 'major rule.' A 'major rule' is defined as one that OMB finds has resulted in or is likely to result in (1) an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more, (2) a major increase in costs or prices for consumers or industries, or (3) significant adverse effects on competition, employment, investment, productivity, innovation, or U.S. competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will submit the interim final rule and technical amendments to OMB for this determination and will submit the appropriate report to Congress and the Government Accountability Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and transition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim final rule and technical amendments are effective April 1, 2024. Many substantive provisions of the 2023 CRA Final Rule become applicable on January 1, 2026, and reporting requirements on January 1, 2027, per § __.51(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies explained the reasons for setting these effective and applicability dates (to provide timely certainty, to align CRA Notice applicability, and to allow transition time for compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCC correction to UMRA expenditure estimates and transition cost conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction to the OCC's UMRA discussion clarifies estimated expenditures if full compliance were required within the first 12 months; under the final rule transition provisions (longer compliance deadlines to January 1, 2026/2027), the OCC concludes the final rule will not result in expenditures of $100 million or more in any one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correction provides the OCC's adjusted estimate breakdown (e.g., $7.9M increased data collection/reporting; $82M for large banks to collect/maintain/report deposit geographic data; $1.9M for banks' strategic plan submissions) and explains how extended transition reduces aggregated annual expenditures.
